newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore-based rubber consumers engage in buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore-based rubber consumers engage in buying.

text.p: Several major rubber companies in Singapore were said to have bought SIR20 rubber on Friday although action for other rubber grades remained thin ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
"I heard that at least one major end-user concluded a deal this afternoon," a source said, adding it was likely most of the purchases were for SIR20 rubber.
The price of the purchase was not available although recent offers for SIR20 ranged between 48 and 49 U.S. cents a lb.
Another trader said: "I heard some of the major consumers did something this afternoon."
Dealers were uncertain whether one of the companies involved in the buying was Bridgestone, which had been seeking offers for SIR20 rubber for most of the past two weeks.
Thai producers were also trying to unload some material in the market ahead of the long Songkran holidays in that country.
"The Thai producers are keen to sell," one dealer said.

At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 115.00-116.00 U.S. cents a kg from 116.00 cents. October/December RSS1 was seen at 170.00 Singapore cents (US$1.18) a kg from 170.50 cents. June TSR20 was seen at 157.00 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from 157.25 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
